Parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio test for nested mixture models

Source: R/enumeration.R
bootstrap_lrt.Rd

bootstrap_lrt() tests whether a more flexible model improves on a simpler one nested in it, typically one more profile or group class. The statistic is twice the difference in maximised log likelihoods; its null distribution is simulated by generating data from the fitted null model and refitting both models to each data set, since the chi-squared approximation does not hold when the number of mixture components changes. A small p-value is evidence against the null in favour of this alternative; it does not say the alternative has the right number of classes.

Usage

bootstrap_lrt(
  null_model,
  alternative_model,
  data = NULL,
  iter = 199L,
  n_starts = NULL,
  max_iter = NULL,
  tol = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

null_model

A converged fit under the null: a profile or class model with or without membership covariates, an lta() fit, or a group-class family fit from multilpa(). See Supported comparisons.

alternative_model

A converged, more flexible model fitted to the same data, in which null_model is nested.

data

The data frame both models were fitted to. Required for transition models, whose simulations keep the observed groups, occasions and covariates; otherwise taken from the fits when omitted, and checked against them when supplied.

iter

Number of simulated data sets (default 199; at least 2). More replicates reduce the Monte Carlo error of the p-value but do not cure estimation problems.

n_starts, max_iter, tol

Controls for each simulated refit; NULL (default) keeps each model's own controls and search strategy. A supplied value applies to both models.

seed

Optional integer seed. The caller's random-number state is restored on exit.

Value

A multilpa_bootstrap_lrt object: the observed statistic, the bootstrap p-value and its Monte Carlo standard error, n_valid and n_invalid replicates, fixed (the measurement blocks held in every refit) and per-replicate diagnostics, including how many starts of each refit replicated its best likelihood. as.data.frame() returns the one-row test summary, get_results(result, "replicates") one row per replicate, summary() both, and plot() the simulated distribution with the observed statistic.

Supported comparisons

Both models must be of one kind: profile or class models, transition models, or group-class family fits. Profile and class models, with or without membership covariates, must differ by exactly one profile (class) or exactly one group class, and share their observations, group layout, covariance structure, centring and scaling, missing-data handling and drop_empty. centering = "grand" is repeated in each refit; person-centred or person-scaled fits are refused, because the model gives the group means removed by those transformations no distribution. Covariate models must share their covariates and slope specification (a one-group-class null may be compared with an alternative that adds group covariates or group-class-specific slopes); covariates are held at their observed values when simulating, and both originals must be fully converged, logits included.

Transition models may differ in class counts or in restrictions on measurement, transitions, Markov order or covariate effects, with compatible indicators, grouping, occasion layout and measurement distributions. Group-class family fits may differ in the number of group classes or in restrictions on the means and variance components, the alternative being the less restricted one. A profile or class fit with fixed (including a fit_staged() result) keeps the same held blocks in every replicate, so the p-value is conditional on that measurement solution; a covariate fit's held blocks are re-estimated in each replicate. Fits with a prior, sampling weights or a noise component are refused.

Calculation

The p-value is (1 + b) / (V + 1), with b the number of valid simulated statistics at least as large as the observed one and V the number of valid replicates. A replicate is invalid when a refit fails or does not converge, or when the alternative's likelihood falls below the null's beyond numerical tolerance; such replicates are left out with a warning, and the p-value is NA when fewer than half of the requested replicates are valid. Leaving them out conditions the reference distribution on successful estimation. Report the invalid share, and look at whether the refits replicated their likelihoods across starts. For covariate models a refit counts as converged when its likelihood has converged even if a membership logit is still moving, as happens with an empty or separated class in the alternative; logits_settled records whether the logits converged too.

Fits with missing = "fiml" are supported when both models use it; each simulated data set keeps the original missing-value pattern. That is calibrated only when missingness is independent of the indicators and the classes given any fixed covariates: a fixed pattern does not reproduce an MAR mechanism that depends on observed indicators, nor an MNAR one, so valid FIML estimation does not by itself make this test valid.

See also

enumerate_classes() for fitting the candidates; compare_models() for information-criterion comparisons.

Examples

set.seed(1)
example_data <- data.frame(
  school = rep(seq_len(10), each = 10),
  score = rnorm(100, rep(c(-2, 2), each = 50))
)
smaller <- multilpa(example_data, "score", "school", n_profiles = 1,
                    n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
larger <- multilpa(example_data, "score", "school", n_profiles = 2,
                   n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
# `iter` is small so the example runs quickly; use many more for inference.
comparison <- bootstrap_lrt(smaller, larger, iter = 9, n_starts = 1,
                            max_iter = 2000, tol = 1e-6, seed = 1)
comparison
#> Parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio comparison
#> Null: 1 profile; alternative: 2 profiles
#> Observed statistic: 44.198110
#> p-value: 0.1 (Monte Carlo SE 0.0949) from 9 of 9 valid replicates (0 invalid)
